content:
The Hidden Async Mistake That Quietly Slowed Every API Request

5 min read
Just now

--

We didn’t change our infrastructure.
We didn’t add a new feature.
We didn’t increase traffic.
We added one innocent-looking await.
Our average API latency jumped from 82 ms to 247 ms almost overnight.
At first, we blamed the database.
Then Redis.
Then networking.
Everything looked healthy.
The culprit turned out to be a single line of code.
Well… not exactly.
The real problem wasn’t the await keyword—it was what we chose to wait for.
This experience taught our team one of the most valuable performance lessons in backend development: protect your request’s critical path.
Everything Looked Fine
Our endpoint was simple.
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<OrderDto> Get(int id)
{
var order = await _repository.GetOrder(id); return order;
}
Production metrics were excellent.
